title: A Sudden Corner Where I Talk About What I've Been Thinking Regarding My More Recent Characters

sections.heading: SHIMAMURA HŌGETSU
sections.content:
"Recent…? Is she really one of my recent characters?"

A fair question to open with, considering she's a ten-year veteran by this point. At this rate, she might even make it to fifteen. If I ranked my protagonists by serialization length, she'd actually be the oldest among all of my works—a true senior. She's worked hard to earn that position.

The image I always associate with her is Asap Suzuki's pose on the cover of The Wings of Rean DVD Volume 1.[ref:wing-of-rean]

"...What do you mean you don't know what that is?"

I've mentioned this somewhere before, but the protagonist of Adachi and Shimamura is Shimamura. Personally, I've never really thought of Adachi as the protagonist.

The reason is pretty simple: to be completely honest, writing from Adachi's perspective is much harder than writing from Shimamura's.

Especially during their school years, Adachi's inner world revolves almost entirely around Shimamura. She has so little emotional room to spare and is constantly wound so tightly that, as the series goes on, writing her perspective becomes increasingly difficult.

That said, Adachi's view of love—or rather, what she seeks from the person most precious to her—may very well lie at the foundation of how love is portrayed throughout my works.

I think "everyone getting along" is an ideal people like to talk about, but not necessarily the answer.

Though, personally, I wouldn't even call it an ideal. That's just conventional wisdom.

This was supposed to be Shimamura's section, yet I ended up writing mostly about Adachi instead.

Still, I think Shimamura would forgive me.

She's that kind of person.

sections.heading: ADACHI SAKURA
sections.content:
"Recent…? Well, she's certainly the very modern heroine of Adachi and Shimamura."

The reason her personality feels different at the very beginning is because the original short story was published in a magazine as a standalone work. At the time, there were absolutely no plans for a continuation.

And yet, here we are—more than ten years later, still walking alongside her.

Whenever I think of Adachi, I picture her walking toward the light. She's by no means a cheerful person, but there's something about the way her heart always moves straight toward whatever she's chosen that creates that image.

Since I already ended up writing quite a bit about Adachi in Shimamura's section, I don't really have much left to say here.

Though I doubt Adachi would mind.

It's less that she'd forgive me and more that she'd simply be indifferent.

By the way, this whole series of posts is partly just me organizing my own thoughts about what each of these characters are like.

references.title: The Wings of Rean
references.note: This refers to The Wings of Rean (Rean no Tsubasa), a six-episode original video animation released between 2005 and 2006 and directed by Yoshiyuki Tomino. Adapted from Tomino's 1983 novel of the same name, The Wings of Rean follows Asap Suzuki, a Japanese teenager who is transported to the parallel world of Byston Well, a recurring setting in several of Tomino's fantasy works. There, he becomes involved in a conflict between competing factions and pilots an aura-powered humanoid machine known as a 'Nanakijin.' The series blends fantasy, mecha, and coming-of-age elements and is generally regarded as a relatively niche entry within Tomino's body of work.
